Which statement is correct?
A
The car accelerates for 2 s, then stops for 4 s and then reverses.
B
The car accelerates at 12 m s–2 for 2 s.
C
The car travels a distance of 36 m in the first 4 s.
D
The car travels a distance of 48 m in the last 4 s.

hints: Notice the shape from 0 to 2 s, 2 s to 6 s and 6 s to 10 s, and that velocity stays at or above zero with a peak of $12 \text{m s}^{-1}$.
Recall that on a velocity-time graph gradient is acceleration and area under the graph is distance travelled.
Split the first 4 s into the 0 to 2 s triangle plus the 2 s to 4 s rectangle, and split the last 4 s from 6 s to 10 s as a triangle to compare areas.
walkthrough: Read the graph: velocity rises linearly from $0$ to $12 \text{m s}^{-1}$ in $0$ to $2 \text{ s}$, stays at $12 \text{m s}^{-1}$ from $2$ to $6 \text{ s}$, then falls linearly to $0$ at $10 \text{ s}$.
Use the velocity-time rules: gradient $= a = \Delta v / \Delta t$ and distance $=$ area under the graph.
Check acceleration: $a = (12-0)/2 = 6 \text{m s}^{-2}$, so the $12 \text{m s}^{-2}$ claim is wrong.
Calculate distance in first $4 \text{ s}$ as two areas: triangle $0$ to $2 \text{ s}$ gives $0.5 \times 2 \times 12 = 12 \text{ m}$, rectangle $2$ to $4 \text{ s}$ gives $2 \times 12 = 24 \text{ m}$.

Add them: $12 + 24 = 36 \text{ m}$ with unit $\text{m}$, confirming the first $4 \text{ s}$ statement. The last $4 \text{ s}$ triangle is only $0.5 \times 4 \times 12 = 24 \text{ m}$. This is option C

A.explanation: From 2 s to 6 s velocity stays at $12 \text{m s}^{-1}$, so the car moves at constant velocity, not stopped, and velocity never goes negative so it never reverses.

B.explanation: Acceleration is the gradient, $(12-0)/2 = 6 \text{m s}^{-2}$, not $12 \text{m s}^{-2}$.

C.explanation: Area under the graph from 0 to 4 s is $12 \text{ m} + 24 \text{ m} = 36 \text{ m}$, which matches the stated distance.

D.explanation: From 6 s to 10 s the area is a triangle $0.5 \times 4 \times 12 = 24 \text{ m}$, not $48 \text{ m}$.
